content:
This is no mystery, but I have (or should I say, _had_ ?) a project of formalizing enough linear algebra in Mathlib so that the classical groups exist over arbitrary fields, together with their simplicity statements, up to establishing one direction of the classification of finite simple groups (minus the 26 sporadic ones which Yael @Bhavik Mehta started tackling).

Now that this is autoformalized by one or two groups, I have several options, ranging from ignoring the autoformalized part (the most reasonable thing to do, IMO) to starting from it (which utterly disgusts me). But I don't know, it might be wiser to just quit this project.

Waiting for your reflexions on this matter.
I think you should simply ignore the auto-formalized stuff and do it right.

@Antoine Chambert-Loir as you know I am not anti AI (though I respect your opinion), but I just consider your goal very different from what these projects do. I understand it's a bit sad to work to put in mathlib your work when you know that someone else already formalized the full thing, but I also think that doing it the right way is absolutely worth, and we want all these results in mathlib.

My last interaction with Mathlib was 3-4 months ago, and I remember an overwhelming impression that Mathlib was pushed in numerous directions at once without all the necessary forces to sustain that. (Of course, everybody who does not their fair load of reviews is partly responsible for that, comprising myself.)

In any case, I believe people in my situation will need formal statements from Mathlib maintainers to be sure that their work is more or less within Mathlib's roadmap.
I think this is an important question that will arise more and more frequently. I’ll make sure this is discussed among Mathlib maintainers.
(what sporadic groups am I tackling? Are you thinking of @Bhavik Mehta ?)
Possibly :hot_pepper: but maybe mathlib too should have roadmaps, and we should close PRs that do not fit an existing roadmap?
Sorry, I meant bhavik and I'll edit.

Patrick Massot said:

I think you should simply ignore the auto-formalized stuff and do it right.

And indeed, personally my attitude is that now that it has been done once, there is no pressure do "just get it done". So we can really do it right. No longer just "take the canonical textbook and work through it", but really slow down, think through correct generalizations/abstractions, think about the engineering aspects in Lean, etc...

Yaël Dillies said:

Possibly :hot_pepper: but maybe mathlib too should have roadmaps

Something along these lines (in the positive sense, i.e. "we'll appreciate contributions here and here") has been discussed. When we get public maintainer meeting minutes (on my agenda, hopefully soon!) you can even read the discussion there. So, I think this part is definitely possible.

we should close PRs that do not fit an existing roadmap

To some extent, this is uncontroversial (e.g., we'd direct a PR about combinatorial games to combinatorial-games-theory, similarly about e.g. physlib or cslib, may close a PR defining superabundant numbers, etc.)
In a broader sense, I don't think this is realistic. (This is my personal opinion, not my MI opinion.) There are many different opinions by the maintainers here; I'd be surprised to see consensus in this direction.

That said, I'm not sure what exactly you mean, Yael: can you elaborate, please?

I'm sure you're putting careful thought into it, but I'd be sad if this precludes the sort of small contributions that more infrequent contributors like myself make. If you look through my commits none are particularly mathematical or would fit on a bigger roadmap. They're little bits of cleaning up at the edge of the library, or API that I needed in CSLib and took the time to upstream because I felt a responsibility to give back in this way.
Not sure who "you" refers to: I certainly think such clean-up is valuable and should (continue to) be welcome.
Sorry, I didn't mean to put words in your mouth! By "you" I meant the maintainers broadly, and just that I have pretty high confidence in that group carefully discussing potential policies like this.
The way Tau Ceti works, small cleanups here and there as you describe are allowed, even if they do not fit a specific roadmap
So far I’ve been ignoring the stuff about elliptic curves in Tau Ceti and trying to do everything carefully myself at the generality I’m (and hopefully others are) satisfied with

@Antoine Chambert-Loir I had the same discussion with @Floris van Doorn some weeks back concerning our Sobolev spaces project, since I saw they appeared on TauCeti. I was sceptical about what to do (and sad), and he gave me a wonderful answer: thanks to this stuff being autoformalised, nobody will put undue pressure on us and we'll be able to do them as we want. I understand your frustration, but I would just ignore the other two projects.

Michael Rothgang said:

That said, I'm not sure what exactly you mean, Yael: can you elaborate, please?

I elaborated for the duration of my plane journey; apologies for the wall of text :speak_no_evil:: https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/287929-mathlib4/topic/Roadmaps.20and.20the.20growth.20of.20mathlib/with/629544830
